description: Drop the stale absolute line-number suffix from the US-R1-002 patterns.md citation, making the pointer a rot-proof content reference.

userStories.title: Make the US-R1-002 patterns.md citation rot-proof by dropping its stale line number
userStories.description: As a reader of the knowledge layer, I need the US-R1-002 bullet in scripts/cam/patterns.md to point at the recordedSleeps.every assertion by its grep-able content instead of the stale absolute line number test/dispatch.test.ts:769, so the pointer resolves correctly and stops rotting every time the test file shifts above it.
acceptanceCriteria: The stale absolute-line citation test/dispatch.test.ts:769 no longer appears anywhere in scripts/cam/patterns.md; the US-R1-002 bullet's pointer to the recordedSleeps.every assertion is now a rot-proof grep-able content reference. [oracle: ! grep -qF 'test/dispatch.test.ts:769' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The US-R1-002 bullet still anchors its pointer on the assertion's content, so the reference stays resolvable after the line-number suffix is dropped. [oracle: grep -qF 'recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The content reference resolves against the real test file: the cited assertion genuinely exists in test/dispatch.test.ts. [oracle: grep -qF 'recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)' test/dispatch.test.ts]

No new absolute line number was frozen for this pointer: the derive-don't-freeze rule is honored (the fix is not :769 changed to another :NNN). The sibling US-003 bullet and its citations, including its separately-tracked stale test/dispatch.test.ts:754, are untouched. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: Single-file doc-only edit to scripts/cam/patterns.md; NO rebuild (patterns.md is not sidecar-executed), no code/test file changes. Target: the US-R1-002 bullet, currently at patterns.md:911 (issue title's :909 is already drifted -- grep, do not trust the number). Change: delete the `:769` suffix from the token `test/dispatch.test.ts:769` so the pointer becomes a content reference; the bullet already quotes the assertion inline (recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)), which is the anchor. Live assertion is at test/dispatch.test.ts:777 (issue's proposed :778 was itself stale -- do NOT reintroduce any number). Sibling US-003 bullet at patterns.md:907 carries test/dispatch.test.ts:754 (a HISTORICAL/main-referencing citation, separately tracked) -- OUT OF SCOPE, must not be touched. Gotchas: derive-don't-freeze (patterns.md:903) forbids re-freezing a new :NNN; never target scripts/cam/handoff.json as an evidence oracle (patterns.md:909, rotating artifact) -- all oracles here target durable surfaces (patterns.md, test/dispatch.test.ts). These two rules were violated by the CAM-376 PRD's own criteria and cost that cycle all three review rounds.
